title: Preserve partial progress when a VCF Operations log-forwarder replacement fails
prompt:
Implement `forwarderreplace/client.go` as a standard-library-only Go 1.22+ client for a two-step VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 VCF Operations Log Management change.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json`, `docs/official_sources.json`, and `forwarderreplace/types.go` first. The focused contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/log-management-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. The JSON specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly operationIds `createLogForwarder` and `deleteLogForwarder`, in that order, and contact no other route.

Preserve the public API and reporting types in `forwarderreplace/types.go`:

- `NewClient(Config) (*Client, error)` validates without traffic. `BaseURL` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no user information, non-root path, query, forced query, or fragment. `Token` must be nonblank, have no surrounding whitespace, and contain no CR or LF. A nil `HTTPClient` means an independent copy of `http.DefaultClient`; otherwise copy the supplied client. Disable redirects on the copy and never mutate caller-owned client state.
- `(*Client).ReplaceLogForwarder(context.Context, string, LogForwarderCreate) (ReplaceResult, error)` rejects a nil context and an empty retired-forwarder id before traffic. First invoke `POST /api/v2/logs/forwarders`. Only after an accepted create response, invoke `DELETE /api/v2/logs/forwarders/{id}`, encoding the old id as one UTF-8 path segment. Do not retry, compensate, or roll back either step.
- Return the truthful `ReplaceResult` on every path. Each `StepOutcome` names its exact operationId and says whether it was attempted, succeeded, and which HTTP status was received (zero when none was received). If create succeeds, retain the decoded `Created` value even when delete later fails. A create failure leaves delete unattempted. The returned `*Error` must identify the exact failing operation and step.

Wire fidelity is strict. Send exactly one `Accept: application/json` and one `X-JWT-Token` on both operations. Send exactly one `Content-Type: application/json` on POST and no `Content-Type` on DELETE. Send no query or bare `?`; DELETE has no body. Serialize writable fields in the exact order of `components.schemas.LogForwarder.properties`, as declared by `LogForwarderCreate`. Omit only nil fields. Preserve explicitly present false, zero, empty string, empty map, and empty JSON object values. Emit compact UTF-8 JSON without a trailing newline or HTML escaping. The read-only `id` property is never part of the request body.

Accept exactly HTTP 201 with an `application/json` JSON object for create and exactly HTTP 204 with an empty body for delete. Bound every response read to 1 MiB. Reject null, arrays, scalars, malformed JSON, trailing data, wrong media types, nonempty 204 bodies, and oversized success bodies as `*Error` with `KindProtocol`. Any received non-success response is `KindHTTP`; a failure before any response is `KindTransport`. Keep context cancellation discoverable through `errors.Is`, but do not expose the token, response body, or underlying transport text. Always close response bodies.

Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`. The protected verifier is table-driven. `internal/contractmock` loads `docs/contract.json`, derives its complete two-operation route allow-list, normally binds only to an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` listener, and writes a synchronized, flushed, fsynced JSONL request log that the tests read. If the sandbox prohibits socket creation, the same handler runs through a contract-derived request-level fallback. In the main scenario create succeeds and delete returns HTTP 404; the verifier proves that the created forwarder and successful create outcome are still reported alongside the exact delete failure. It also asserts exact method, escaped request target, header multiplicity, compact body bytes and property order, explicit falsy-value preservation, omission of every unset optional field including read-only `id`, response validation, pre-I/O validation, redirect refusal, caller-client immutability, and refusal to serve unnamed operations. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

`go.mod`, everything under `docs/`, `internal/contractmock/server.go`, `forwarderreplace/types.go`, and `forwarderreplace/client_test.go` are protected. Edit only `forwarderreplace/client.go`. Do not add dependencies, install or download tools, use subprocesses or raw sockets, or vendor, intercept, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware SDKs, specifications, or harness tools.
scenario: A replacement log forwarder is created successfully, but retiring the old forwarder returns HTTP 404; callers must receive the created resource and exact successful first-step outcome together with the later-step failure.
constraint: The contract-derived loopback allow-list contains only createLogForwarder and deleteLogForwarder, while its durable request log proves exact wire shape, nil-field omission, explicit falsy-value preservation, and correct ordering.
